Trial #1: New plan: I failed because I treated every room entry as a unique node, resulting in duplicate entries (e.g., "Bedroom" appearing three times) and an inflated graph that did not represent the actual topology. I did not track which *locations* I had already visited, only the sequence of steps. Next time, I will maintain a set of unique room names to identify visited locations. When entering a room, I will check if its name is already in my `nodes` list; if it is, I will not add it again and will instead update the `edges` to reflect the new connection to the existing node. I will only call "DONE" when the set of unique visited rooms equals the total number of distinct rooms encountered, ensuring no duplicates exist in the final graph.
